title: Fondukistan monastic annex
geometryBasis: Primary DAFA written monastic room functions with original estimated south-side annex layout.
sectionBasis: Estimated historical monastic cells, meeting hall and common rooms adjoining the distinct sanctuary. Written room functions are archaeological facts; dimensions, eight-cell census, sections and south-side layout are original reconstruction estimates. DAFA written excavation description confirms sanctuary plus cells, meeting hall and common rooms. Eight cells, their arrangement around a small court, all widths/heights/roof profiles, doors, materials and precise700CEcondition are original estimates; no excavation plan, photo or artwork supplied geometry. This is a plausible structural interpretation, not an archaeological survey. The annex centre is estimated22m south of the unchanged sanctuary point. Modern coarse terrain is acquired before sections; each small room begins on a stepped masonry plinth above its corner samples. Original sourcefield is retained without flattening or masking. Historical bench depths and plinths are visualization estimates; no verified seventh-century vertical tie. Four levels retain all ten estimated rooms, actual door openings, flat roofs and terraced plinths; district and closer levels retain parapets. Near levels add timber beam ends, lintels and slight roof lips. Plain adobe, lime plaster, rammed earth and timber are original material interpretations. No decoration or artifact replicas.
